Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 11/04/2025
Comments: On site today (06:00) to follow up on the incident that occurred during stimulation operations of the Lauer 12H well on (10/22/25). Met with Operators Drilling and Completions Superintendent (Steve Brominski) to go over operators plan for removal and replacement of the 12H 13 3/8" well head today. Operations will start at first light. ~ 07:00 - 07:15 - Safety meeting held with all parties involved. ~ 08:00 - 450 ton crane arrived and began rigging up. Crane will be used to pull back Production casing. CUDD/ Cactus Well Services: ~ 08:30 - 09:30 - cut well head off the 13 3/8" and 9 5/8" casings ~ 10:00 - 10:30 - cut 13 3/8" casing to required length for new well head ~ 11:00 - 11:20 - cut 9 5/8" casing to required length for new well head ~ 11:30 - landed spear in 5 1/2" production casing and pulled casing back to a 20" stick up in order to insure casing will be able to be pulled back inside new tubing head and slips set ~ 11:45 - landed casing head (to be welded to 13 3/8" casing) ~ 12:10 - landed tubing head and torqued to the casing head ~ 13:15 - speared Production casing and pulled back thru tubing head and set slips ~ 13:45 - cut 5 1/2" casing to required length ~ 14:00 - set well cap and torqued down The back side of Production casing will be plumbed w/ a pressure gauge to monitor any developing pressure. - An e-mail sent by Operator at 17:38 (11/4/25) to the Dept. confirmed all pack-off and annular seals were successfully tested. The Lauer 12H well is now fully secure.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/05/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/05/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8248044
Permit API: 123-47821
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2025
Comments: The Loomis B Lease Loomis 7 OG well is the closest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the Loomis B lease. At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the Loomis 7 OG well. The Loomis B tank battery consists of two stock tanks, a produced fluids separator, and one subsurface produced fluids tank located inside earthen containment diking. The conventional wells on this lease were being produced at the time of this inspection. After arriving on the lease I began to inspect the condition of the tank battery. I found that the produced fluids separator and stock tanks in containment were equipped with PVC drain lines to separate any produced fluids that enter the tank battery from either the separator or the stock tanks into the subsurface produced fluids tank. At the time of this inspection, only the PVC drain line connected to the separator was found to be draining produced fluids. At the time of this inspection, the flowing PVC drain line was improperly positioned, as it was straddled on the edge of a cutout hole on the top of the subsurface produced fluids tank. The manner in which the drain line was situated allows the majority of the fluids flowing through the line to be released onto the top of the tank and ultimately onto the floor of the containment area, as opposed to inside the subsurface tank.The specific conductance of the accumulated fluid inside of the containment area measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. The soils below the fluid accumulating in the containment area also measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. A visual inspection of the containment area revealed additional signs of staining and stressed/dead vegetation around the produced fluids tank similar to that resulting from the ongoing release. This evidence is an indication of previous releases inside of the containment area prior to this inspection. At the time of this inspection, it did not appear that the pooling of fluids around the subsurface produced fluids tank were accumulating at a rate consistent with the volume of fluids being released into containment by the PVC drain. This and the evidence of stressed vegetation/oil staining around the proximity of the subsurface produced fluids tank referenced above suggests that the released fluids inside of the containment area are migrating into the soil below. A conservative estimate of a one gallon per minute discharge rate over the greater than 90 minute duration that I was present to observe the release suggests that more than 90 gallons (>2bbl) were released into the containment during this inspection.Sample number 4568-004 was collected from the fluid actively flowing from the PVC drain line and sample number 4568-005 was collected from the accumulated fluids inside of the containment area adjacent the subsurface produced fluids tank. These samples were sent to the DEP lab for SAC 942 analyses. After concluding my inspection, I called Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) at 14:59 and requested that he meet me immediately on the lease. Upon his arrival, I informed Kyle that I discovered a problem with the tank battery. I gestured to the ongoing release of fluids from the improperly placed PVC drain line. Kyle immediately placed the drain line into the cutout in the subsurface produced fluids tank. Kyle then phoned another TMP official to inform them of the release, but indicated that neither he or the other TMP official seemed to be aware of who had pumped the wells on this lease today. I informed Kyle that the release of fluids would be documented in this inspection report and that a Notice of Violations (NOV) would be included.A NOV is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: Brody Webster, contacted Gene Rickard by phone on March 17, 2020 at 4:27 PM to report that a spill had occurred on COG's Davis G Well Pad located in Gibson Township, Susquehanna County. The spill had occurred on March 14, 2020 at 10:00 AM while a service rig (Consolidated Wellsite Services) was on location to remove the 2 3/8-inch production tubing from the 2H well. During the operation, it was determined that there was debris (sand, shale fragments, etc.) within the production tubing causing fluid (primarily freshwater that had been introduced to the well) to be retained inside the pipe as it was brought to the surface. As each 30' segment of tubing was recovered and separated at the threaded connection, the fluid was drained from the pipe to the sealed well cellar (6' diameter metal cellar with cement base) and subsequently recovered by vacuum truck. During the process, a limited volume of the fluid sprayed/misted outside of the cellar and impacted an area of soil near the 2H well cellar. Approximately 7 to 8 cubic yards of visibly impacted soils were excavated and placed into a lined roll-off container for off-site disposal at an approved facility. Resource Environmental has been contracted to characterize the remaining soils. The reason the 2 3/8-inch pipes held water was because it was discovered that the pipe was plugged at the bottom by sand and other debris. Probably the reason for the pipes removal in the first place. The spill volume was reported as 22 gallons of produced and freshwater mixed together.

Comments: On 3/23/2026, an inspection was conducted in response to reported sloughing (IR 4163547) at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. The sloughing was reportedly discovered by the operator on 3/20/2026, on the cutslope above the access road. Range Resources representative Denny Furmanek was present at the start of this inspection. An Individual Erosion and Sedimentation permit (ESP) was issued by the Department for this site on 1/26/2024 and expires on 1/25/2029.The following was observed during the inspection:The sloughing was observed on the cutslope above the access road, as reported by the operator on 3/20/2026 (photos 3-6). This area appears to be approximately 15 feet in width and does not appear to immediately threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. No pipeline markers and/or gas well equipment were observed below the slough. Temporary stabilization is applied to the slough. Furmanek reported that no additional soil movement has occurred since the slough was discovered. Repairs are reportedly expected to begin once the ground dries adequately to allow for machine operation. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 7). Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMP) appear to be constructed in the locations shown on the approved ESP plan drawings (photos 15-21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) inspection log, and ESP approval letter are on site (photos 2-5). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 12). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photos 24 and 25). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units on site are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 13 and 14). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the slough on the cutslope above the access road.The following information is requested from the operator:- What is being done in the interim (temporary stabilization)- What is being done in the future (permanent stabilization)Please coordinate with DEP Technical Services for any potential modifications to the approved ESP that may be necessary for addressing the slough.

Comments: On January 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. At the time of inspection, contractors where excavating the area in front of the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the well pad. The depth of the excavation was about 4 to 5 ft. The area of the infiltration berm that had yet to be excavated had a conductivity greater than 4,000 uS/cm. The design of the trench along the west end of the pad caused production fluid to flow to the southwest corner also. The southwest area of the pad also has a drainage culvert with the outlet pipe draining to the infiltration berm. The pooled production fluid in the northwest infiltration berm has been vacuumed out. The conductivity of the soil in front of that infiltration berm was over 4,000 uS/cm. No excavation has been done to this area. The northwest plunge pool filled back with water. The conductivity of the water was over 4,000 uS/cm. A sample was collected from the plunge pool and will be analyzed for SAC code 942. Mr. Rodriguez thinks that the seal around the outlet pipe from the drainage culvert in that area is failing, resulting in water in the plunge pool. There were no new seeps or areas where the production fluid has appeared off the well pad edge. STL Resources plans to finish removing the impacted soil from the southwest infiltration berm and move to the northwest infiltration berm to begin removing impacted soil there. Mr. Rodriguez said that a vacuum truck was scheduled to vacuum out the water in the northwest plunge pool and the water that had drained into the culverts from the trench along the west end of the pad. The spill of production fluid off the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 401. Clean Streams Law 402(b) is being supplanted by Clean Streams Law 401. Violations from Inspection Report 3305227 remain outstanding.

Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. A follow-up inspection found that the liquid crude oil/water mix that was in the secondary containment has been removed. There is ice and snow covering most of the bottom of the secondary containment making it unclear as to the extent of the clean-up however the ice around the tanks appears to be clear and does not contain any residual oil contamination. An empty plastic 200 gallon is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. A follow-up inspection will be completed when there is a thaw and the stone in the secondary containment can be inspected for contamination. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-019 collected on 7/18/2024 at 11:57 AM as part of inspection report #3798130 at the Tract 726 D Pad. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-019 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Aluminum - 1.6 mg/L; Barium - 11.0 mg/L; Strontium- 1.44 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- >3,230 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 600.6 mg/L (photos 1 and 2). PGE submitted an NOV response letter to the Department on August 2, 2024 which stated the following actions were taken regarding the Department's 7/18/2024 inspection: "PGE had a vac truck take up the puddled fluid immediately. A 50 X 15 X > 3 deep area of soil was then dug up and loaded into a lined roll off for sampling and disposal. PGE asserts that it was not in violation of any state or federal regulation nor was PGE acting contrary to the permit issued under the authority of the Department. It cannot be established that the puddled fluid was caused solely by any activity conducted by PGE rather than a combination of mat washing and heavy rainfall."In follow-up inspection #3801042, the Department verified that impacted material was being scraped from the site and placed into a lined rolloff container for sampling. As the volume of pollutional material released to the pad surface has not been measured or quantified, the Department recommends PGE pursue Act 2 remediation response in accordance with 78a.66. Violations noted.

Comments: At time of inspection: On site for a post-plugging inspection of the Phoenix 590796 (117-20970) well to confirm the current condition of this previously leaking plugged well. I met with EQT's EHS Supervisor Rick Hall. A crew was on site to clean out the cellar to locate the (13x9) annulus and vent it to the surface. The plugged well was open and vented (see photo #1). There was water at the bottom of the cellar with intermittent bubbling noticed (see photo #2), gas was detected at 41% LEL and 2% CH4. The casing was full of water and there was no bubbling noticed when I arrived on site. The well started bubbling in the 9 5/8" casing (see photo #3), there was gas detected at 100% LEL and 41% CH4 in the casing. The bubbling only lasted a short time and there was no bubbling in the casing when I left the site. The 2" valve for the (13x9) annulus was located, the valve was closed with an elbow and pipe leading from the well below grade to an unknown location. They said they would need to remove the cellar to get better access to the line.

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8206966
Permit API: 027-21225
Unconventional: No
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/05/2024
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 027-21225 with Justin Galiolto of DEP and the property owners on November 5, 2024. During the inspection two leaks were identified. A brine leak was observed coming from an open annulus vent on the bottom of the well head (photos 1-3). A hole approximately 2'x2' was observed at the drip. Large rocks were placed in this hole. I screened the area using a Hanna soil probe and got a blinking reading of 4.0 mS/cm. The soil probe max's out at 4.0 mS/cm.The second leak was observed coming from where the brine pipe attaches to the brine tank near of the top of the 50 BBL tank (pictures 4-5). A wet black streak was observed running down the side of the brine tank was well. Please note that the brine tank was full of fluids. A 5X Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were observed. I contacted Heather Empfield of Diversified Production LLC at ~1230 and made her aware of my findings. At ~1300 Ms. Empfield notified me to let me know Diversified personal were enroute to go investigate the brine leaks. Violations have been cited. Due to the unknown quantity of brine released and unknown amount of time the leaks have been occurring, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 for site remediation.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/11/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/11/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 961507
Permit API: 081-21878
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/11/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after on 6/24/2022, the operator reported a release of 140 barrels of produced fluid to the secondary containment, some of which then overflowed the secondary containment and flowed onto the pad surface. I first inspected Pad B. I met with company man Walt Arnold upon arriving on location. I saw a piece of discarded secondary containment that was sitting on the rig mats for the sandboxes near the pad entrance. Some fluid was dripping off of the containment and onto the rig mats. I asked the company man if there was secondary containment beneath the rig mats and he said no. I recommended to him that the discarded containment be placed on secondary containment until it could be thrown away. He said that he would have someone put it on secondary containment right away. Before I left the pad, the discarded containment was on its own secondary containment. Fluid with a electrical conductivity (EC) of >19.99 mS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter is present on the secondary containment for the blender. The Department recommends vacuuming out the containment. Fluid with an EC of between 1.6 to 2.3 mS/cm was observed on the pad surface near the northeast corner of the pad where some secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The Department recommends scraping up the fluid in this area of the pad. Along the east side of the pad, at the southeast corner of the secondary containment for the produced water tanks, I observed staining and dampness on the pad surface. I also observed the dampness beneath the secondary containment berm as well. The fluid beneath the berm had an EC of >19.99 mS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter. The fluid present inside the containment also had an EC of >19.99 mS/cm. I also got the same reading when I pressed the meter probes into the mud on the pad surface. The visibly impacted area adjacent to the secondary containment was approximately 5 square feet in total. The surface area impacted beneath the secondary containment is unknown. When the berm of the secondary containment was lifted by EQT personnel, the pad surface beneath the containment appeared damp. I took a soil sample from the pad surface adjacent to the containment berm and slightly beneath the berm. There was not enough fluid on the pad surface to take a water sample. The sample is number 0718-196 which will be sent to the state laboratory to be analyzed for SAC 530 + Li and Br. Violations pending sample results.I also met with Rick Hall of EQT during this inspection and I showed him the area where I found the dampness, staining, and fluid at the corner of the produced water secondary containment. Violations remain outstanding for the release on 6/24/2022.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 892715
Permit API: 027-21692
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Twp
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 08/25/2020
Comments: A pre-plugging inspection of this well was conducted August 25, 2020. The well is being replugged to address presence of gas at surface observed after initial plugging. At the time of inspection, the well has 9 5/8" and 5 1/2" casings visible at surface, both open and venting. The 9 5/8" has been welded to the 5 1/2" with a plate and a vent opening. 94% methane was detected at the vent opening with an Altair 5x gas meter. 5 1/2" casing is open and outfitted with welhead flange. Approximately 2% methane was detected inside the 5 1/2". 78.91 violations outstanding at this time. The operator intends to re-enter the wellbore and remediate the well with a squeeze to address the issue. Downhole operations are scheduled to begin next week.

Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/08/2023
Violation Code: 102.5(m)4 - PERMIT REQUIREMENTS – GENERAL PERMITS – Person failed to comply with the terms and conditions of the E & S Control General Permit.
Violation ID: 997793
Permit API: 015-20321
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2023
Comments: On 6/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Solowiej well site. It was 65 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. I did not screen for conductivity because I did not witness any water puddles or muddy areas on the pad surface during the inspection.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by one sediment pond. The sediment pond is adequately stabilized and was dry at the time of the inspection. I was able to witness an 8 inch riser sticking up about 16 inches from the pond surface. The outlet for the sediment pond overflow drains into a stream alongside the River View roadway. This stream drains to the waters of the Commonwealth. Following an inspection conducted on 10/18/2022, Chesapeake reported that it would make changes to the site to mitigate the issues with the sediment pond. They reported that they were developing a design to accommodate both the drainage and the land owner and hoped to have a finalized plan with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features. There are outstanding violations against the outfall coming off the sediment pond. There were three wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake continues with the process to obtain a revised ESCGP application with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features and submit to the Department for review.I left the site at 1400 hours.
